newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen up with JGBs in thin,technical trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen up with JGBs in thin,technical trade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures gained from a rise in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Monday but dealers said activity was largely technically driven in the absence of fresh fundamental factors.
"There was no interest in the trade figures whatsoever," said a dealer with a European futures house, in a reference to data showing a decrease in Japan's October trade surplus.
"Investors stayed on the sidelines. It was mainly dealer-driven and volumes were desperately thin," he added.
The lead June Euroyen contract stood at 99.23 at 1125 GMT against its IMM close at 99.20 on turnover of 8,000 lots. December JGBs settled at 125.38 against their previous 124.74.
The trader said much of the JGB volume was derived from players rolling over their positions to the March contract. "Provided we stay above 124.75, the trend should be reasonably positive," he said.

Dealers said the market would focus increasingly on the Bank of Japan's quarterly "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment, due on November 27, for confirmation Japan's economic recovery was not yet self-sustaining and interest rates were likely to remain
Eurodollar futures ended a listless session scarcely moved, with dealers expecting activity to remain slow due to a relatively thin calendar of economic releases this week.
"Housing starts are possibly the highlight of the week, which is pretty sad," said the trader.
March Eurodollars ended unchanged against their IMM close at 94.49 on volume of a mere 1,625 lots.
